Here's a regex for ISO 8601 calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` matches the year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.
- `^…$` anchors the match to the whole string. Drop the anchors, or use `\b…\b`, to find dates inside longer text.

This checks the format and the ranges, but it doesn't check the calendar. It accepts `2026-02-31`, for example. To reject impossible dates, validate the match with a date parser.

It matches `2026-10-01`.
